page: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v5 is a compute-focused instance within the general-purpose D-series family, distinguished by its reduced memory profile. Built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is absent, requiring external managed disks for file systems and data persistence. The instance includes no GPU accelerators.

Hardware-level vector instruction support includes AVX-512 Foundation and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic hardware acceleration including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. In synthetic performance benchmarks, the processor scored 1624.0 in single-core and 9749.0 in multi-core Geekbench tests, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21165.21 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 15530.57. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 93.58 GB/sec with write throughput measuring 54.98 GB/sec.

Throughput benchmarks demonstrated 20.33 GB/sec in static web serving and 15.59 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. For lightweight machine learning workloads, inference evaluation using a 135M parameter language model achieved 1024.2 prompt processing tokens per second and 237.29 generation tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the low-memory ratio of 2 GB per core allows scaling computational threads without incurring expenses for unneeded RAM. The absence of local disk requires external storage planning for high-IOPS applications. The configuration fits compute-centric workloads requiring high core density with modest memory footprints, including software compilation, batch processing, web serving, and containerized microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ls_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring a 16-vCPU, 8-physical-core Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured with a low-memory profile, it provides 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, with no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. The processor supports AVX-512 VNNI and hardware cryptography instructions, backed by a 48 MB L3 cache. Benchmark evaluations record a Geekbench multi-core score of 9749.0, a PassMark CPU score of 21165.21, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 93.58 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 20.33 GB/sec in static web serving and 15.59 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers cost efficiency for compute-heavy tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity, making it appropriate for software build servers, web frontends, batch computation, and containerized microservices.
